nodes.summary: Let $F_n$ be the free group on generators $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$. A word is a finite list of letters $(i, b)$ with $i < n$ and $b$ a boolean, where $(i, \mathrm{true})$ stands for $x_i$ and $(i, \mathrm{false})$ for $x_i^{-1}$. Given a finite list of words, this is the subgroup of $F_n$ generated by the elements of $F_n$ that the words represent, each word representing the product of its letters.

Then there is an algorithm deciding, for such a list, whether the subgroup $H$ it generates is inert, that is, whether $r(H \cap K) \le r(K)$ for every subgroup $K$ of $F_n$. nodes.title: Inertness is decidable in free groups of finite rank (Kourovka Problem 19.104)

nodes.summary: The statement that for every natural number $n$ there is an algorithm deciding, for a finite list of words in the generators $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ of the free group $F_n$ and their inverses, whether the subgroup of $F_n$ they generate is inert; that is, the predicate on lists of words is computable.

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and all subgroups $H$ and $K$ of the free group $F_n$ on $n$ generators, if $H$ and $K$ are compressed, then $H \cap K$ is compressed. That is, Kourovka Problem 19.103 has a positive answer for the intersection of two subgroups of a free group of finite rank.
